text:
nima: Heads-up: sample-app warmup in staging caused duplicate side-effects when a warmup probe got 429 and SDK retried immediately. Two accounts created for one email.

tara: Yikes. Is warmup using the same idempotency key?

nima: Yes, SDK replays the last request with the same X-Request-Id to prime caches. Server accepted both after transient 429.

sam: Two quick fixes: (1) backend honor an X-Warmup header and skip side-effects; (2) SDK should mark warmup probes and apply jittered backoff/unique id so they don't behave like final retries.

mira: Agreed. Also need telemetry so warmup traffic can be filtered from billing. Metrics like warmup=true tag.

infra-bot: INF-901 created: move dedupe middleware earlier and respect X-Warmup.

tara: SDK parity note: JS replays immediately, Python delays 100ms. Let's standardize: warmup backoff randomized 50-150ms on first retry. Default warmup.enabled=false.

sam: Pseudocode: if warmup.enabled => headers['X-Warmup']='1'; headers['X-Request-Id']=gen_unique(); backoff=random(50,150)ms. Else normal idempotency.

mira: Also update sample-app quickstart to call /warmup-readonly or /health instead of mutation endpoints. Add onboarding checklist line.

tara: I'll own sample-app docs. Sam please open SDK PRs and tag @mira for review.

sam: Will do. Leaving thread for PR links and infra deploy notes.
